title: CAD Drafter
idiom: Victorian steel-engraved machine drawing, one red pen mark for the hole nobody has measured
hero_prompt: Victorian steel-engraved engineering drawing in the manner of a 19th-century machine-design plate, black ink on cream with a single accent of engineering red, hand-made on paper, flat and graphic with visible engraved line and hatching texture, not a photograph, not a 3D render, no depth-of-field, wide panoramic composition: a woman draughtsman in a high-collared blouse seated on a tall stool in profile at a slanted drafting board, her hands folded in her lap, looking at the drawing in front of her; pinned on the board is a precise drawing of a round flanged cap, a section cut through it with fine diagonal hatching, and a circle of bolt holes around it, every hole inked in black except one place where only a small dotted ring in red waits, empty; a pair of bowed outside calipers lies unused on the board beside it and a red pencil rests across the edge. No numerals, no lettering, dimension lines with plain end ticks only.
icon_prompt: Linocut emblem, a flat single-colour black silhouette on an engineering-red ground, no shading or gradients: a pair of bowed outside calipers gripping a thick round disc that has one empty open ring cut out of it. Bold, high-contrast, no fine linework, reads clearly at 24 pixels.
